overview: A two-page U.S. Department of State list of papers indexing correspondence from 1933 and 1937 concerning Japanese government support for shipping. Entries 26–30 describe reports and telegrams from the Embassy in Japan and the consulate at Kobe about ship-construction and mail subsidies, navigation-route appropriations, deep-sea shipping, fast-tonnage construction, relevant Japanese laws and ordinances, budget allocations in yen, and the subsidy income of Osaka Syosen Kaisya. The list also records cross-references to decimal-file subjects 894.712 and 894.642.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Japanese navigation and shipping subsidies
subfiles.about: An index summarizes papers numbered 26–30 concerning Japanese shipping-subsidy laws, appropriations, calculations, and company income.
subfiles.summary: The first page indexes a 1933 Kobe report and June 1937 inquiries and replies concerning ship prices, the availability and uniformity of construction subsidies, mail subsidies, budget provisions, and a requested translation of the new law. The continuation lists Grew's telegram on subsidy laws and yen appropriations, his transmission of Kobe despatch no. 127 with translated legislation and current-budget authorizations, and Gourley's report on Osaka Syosen Kaisya's projected 1938 income from direct subsidies. Several entries were also noted to related decimal-file classifications 894.712 and 894.642.

interest: The list is useful as a compact roadmap to a larger body of diplomatic and consular reporting, preserving document numbers, dates, authors, transmission routes, and cross-references even where the underlying papers are absent. It identifies the precise subsidy categories monitored by U.S. officials and shows their interest in whether Japanese aid was uniformly available across cargo, passenger, and combination vessels. The reference to Osaka Syosen Kaisya's subsidy income also connects national policy to a specific shipping company, while the file-number annotations help historians trace related material elsewhere in the State Department's decimal filing system.
